about: The terms the sources themselves define, mapped by hand to concepts of the index. 'definitions': each definition of the pseudo-Platonic Definitions (Ὅροι), as Burges prints the English heading (page) and as Hermann's Greek prints the headword (OCR as received), with the GLAUx lemma it is indexed under (empty where GLAUx does not tag the word in Plato). The definition quoted is cut by rule: from the heading to the first stop. 'taylor_terms': each entry of Taylor's 'Explanation of Certain Platonic Terms' (1804), by segment. A row whose concept is one of concepts.json adds to it; the others make a concept of their own. 'later': readings of the later Platonists, quoted from Taylor's translations of Plotinus, Proclus' Theology and Iamblichus (Internet Archive OCR, as received), added to a concept.

later.quote: We must conceive a surrounding splendor, proceeding indeed from this cause, but from it in a permanent state, like a light from the sun shining
later.says: Plotinus: what proceeds from the first is like light shining from the sun, the cause abiding unmoved.

later.quote: yet it is a certain image of intellect
later.says: Plotinus: soul is an image of intellect, and must look to it.

later.quote: it is necessary that intellect should look to the highest God, in order that it may be intellect
later.says: Plotinus: intellect is intellect by looking to the first God.

later.quote: a flight of the alone to the alone
later.says: Plotinus, the closing words of the Enneads: the life of the gods and of divine men.

later.quote: temperance is an inward conversion to intellect
later.says: Plotinus, on the virtues: temperance as the soul's turning inward to intellect.

later.quote: This, therefore, is the virtue of the soul, or rather that which happens to it from conversion
later.says: Plotinus: virtue is what comes to the purified soul from its conversion.

later.quote: And if it is so evil, as to be evil itself, it will not participate of good
later.says: Plotinus on matter: what is evil itself has no share in good.

later.quote: there should be an image of the one , and which possesses unity in continuity of succession
later.says: Plotinus on time: an image of the one, a unity spread out in succession.

later.quote: the beautiful itself, and not a certain beauty only
later.says: Plotinus: the lover is to be led to the beautiful itself.

later.quote: who has neither any form nor idea, but is established above intellect and every intelligible
later.says: Porphyry's Life of Plotinus, in Taylor's version: the first God, beyond intellect, which Plotinus reached by the paths of the Symposium.

later.quote: for the one is the same with the good
later.says: Proclus, Theology of Plato: the one is the same as the good.

later.quote: is impartible and uniform, but at the
later.says: Proclus, Theology of Plato: every intellect is impartible and uniform (yet also manifold).

later.quote: It denominates this principle however, the one and the good; by the former of these names indicating its transcendent simplicity
later.says: Taylor's introduction to Iamblichus: the first principle is called the one, for its simplicity, and the good.

later.quote: the ignorance of things honourable and beautiful will be darkness, but the knowledge of them will be light
later.says: Porphyry's letter to Anebo, which Iamblichus answers: ignorance is darkness, knowledge light.

later.quote: the sacred operations pertaining to which called theurgy are here developed
later.says: Taylor's preface: the Mysteries sets out theurgy, the sacred operations of the ancient theology.

later.quote: thus also the human soul is conjoined to them by knowledge
later.says: Iamblichus: the human soul is joined to the gods by knowledge.

scholia.quote: τῷ σώματι χρώμενον ψυχή ἐστι
scholia.says: The scholiast on Alcibiades I 130a: the soul is what uses the body.

scholia.quote: ὅτι ἀρετή τέ ἐστι καὶ ἐπιστήμη τῶν ὄντων
scholia.says: The scholiast on Gorgias 466a: virtue is also knowledge of the things that are.

scholia.quote: καὶ ὅτι ἢ βούλησις ἀεὶ τῶν ἀγαϑῶν ἐστιν
scholia.says: The scholiast on Gorgias 470b: wish is always of good things.

scholia.label: Will, power and intellect (the triad)
scholia.quote: τρία ταῦτά ἐστι περὶ τὰ ὄντα, ἃ ἄνωϑεν ἀρχόμενα μέχρι τῶν ἡμετέρων ἀφικνοῦνται ψυχῶν
scholia.says: The scholiast on Gorgias 471e: three things, wish, power and intellect, reach from above down to our souls, and are seen in the Demiurge.

scholia.quote: μεγαλοπρέπειά ἐστιν ἕξις βελτίστη περὶ δαπάνας
scholia.says: The scholiast on Republic 486a defines magnificence.

scholia.quote: ἐστὶν ἕξις φαύλη περὶ χρήματα, μὴ ἀναλίσκουσα ταῦτα εἰς ἃ δεῖ
scholia.says: The scholiast on Republic 486a defines its opposite, illiberality (ἀνελευθερία).

scholia.quote: ὃ πᾶς χρόνος αἰῶνός ἐστι τοῦ παντὸς εἰκών
scholia.says: The scholiast on Republic 546a: the whole of time is an image of the whole of eternity.

scholia.quote: μέτρον δ᾽ ὃ πᾶς αἰών
scholia.says: The scholiast on Republic 546a: eternity is the measure (of the life of the intelligible).

scholia.quote: σοφιστὴν καλεῖ ὃ Πλάτων καὶ τὸν Ἔρωτα
scholia.says: The scholiast on the Sophist's opening: Plato calls Eros, Hades and Zeus sophists too.

scholia.quote: ἔστι γὰρ κατὰ τὸν μέγαν Ἰάμβλιχον σκοπὸς νῦν περὶ τοῦ ὑπὸ σελήνην δημιουργοῦ
scholia.says: The scholiast, after Iamblichus: the Sophist's subject (skopos) is the demiurge below the moon.

scholia.quote: ϑεὸν μὲν τὸν δημιουργὸν σαφῶς, παλαιὸν δὲ λόγον λέγει τὸν Ὀρφικόν
scholia.says: The scholiast on Laws 715e: 'the god' is plainly the Demiurge, the 'ancient saying' the Orphic one.

scholia.label: Adrasteia (the ordinance of Adrasteia)
scholia.quote: ἡ ᾿Αδράστεια μία ἐστὶ ϑεὸς τῶν μενουσῶν ἐν τῇ νυκτί
scholia.says: The scholiast on Phaedrus 248c: Adrasteia, the goddess who gives the divine laws, born of Providence.

scholia.quote: ἐκ τῆς οὖν προνοίας τῆς ἀκλινοῦς γέγονεν
scholia.says: The scholiast on Phaedrus 248c: Adrasteia comes from unswerving providence.

scholia.quote: διαφέρει δὲ τῆς ἐκεῖ Δίκης
scholia.says: The scholiast on Phaedrus 248c sets Adrasteia apart from Dikē there.

scholia.quote: τὸ μὲν ὀργανικὸν αἴτιον ὃ λόγος ἐστίν
scholia.says: The scholiast on Gorgias 451a: speech (logos) is the instrumental cause of rhetoric.

scholia.quote: πᾶσα γὰρ δύναμις ἄλλου ἐστὶ
scholia.says: The scholiast on Gorgias 456c: every power is the power of something else, its user.

scholia.quote: διὰ ποικιλίας καὶ κινήσεως καὶ τῆς ἐπὶ πᾶν προόδου μεμίμηνται
scholia.says: The scholiast on Gorgias 456a: daemons imitate the simple divine nature by variety, motion and procession.

scholia.quote: διὰ ποικιλίας καὶ κινήσεως καὶ τῆς ἐπὶ πᾶν προόδου μεμίμηνται
scholia.says: The scholiast on Gorgias 456a speaks of procession (πρόοδος) to all things.

scholia.label: The divided line
scholia.quote: Σχόλιον ἐκ τῶν ᾿Αρχύτου καὶ Βροντίνου καὶ Ἰαμβλίχου ἐπιτμηϑέν
scholia.says: The scholion on Republic 509d is drawn from Archytas, Brontinus and Iamblichus.

scholia.quote: λογιστική ἐστι ϑεωρία τῶν ἀριϑμητῶν
scholia.says: The scholiast defines calculation (logistikē): the study of numbered things.

scholia.quote: διὰ τῆς εὐτάκτου κινήσεως τὸν δημιουργόν
scholia.says: The scholiast on Republic 530a: the true astronomer wonders at the Demiurge through the heaven's ordered motion.

scholia.quote: ἡ ἀρετὴ δύναται καὶ ὡς ὅλον εἰς μέρη τὰς ὑπ᾽ αὐτὴν ἀρετὰς διαιρεῖσϑαί
scholia.says: The scholiast on Laws 633a: virtue is divided into the virtues under it, as a whole into parts.

scholia.quote: τοῦ δὲ τελικοῦ αἰτίου τῶν ἠϑικῶν ἀρχῶν
scholia.says: The scholiast on Gorgias 508c: the final cause of the principles of ethics.

scholia.quote: φιλότιμον καὶ ϑυμικὸν
scholia.says: The scholiast on Laws 631b: the honour-loving and spirited kind of soul.

scholia.quote: τὸ γὰρ λογιστικὸν τῆς τοῦ τυράννου ψυχῆς
scholia.says: The scholiast on Republic 577e: the reasoning part of the tyrant's soul, ruled by spirit and desire.
